items.detail: **Wednesday's September CPI** is the week's main event, with forecasts near **3.7% headline**, up from 3.4% in August, as record gasoline prices pass through.
items.why: A hotter print could push the 10-year back toward 5.35% and revive Fed hike bets that faded last week.

items.detail: **TSMC reports Thursday**, guiding to **$44.6–45.8 billion** in revenue, the first hard read on AI chip demand since last week's OpenAI revenue scare.
items.why: Strong AI orders would back the Nasdaq's record at 27,366, while a soft outlook would reopen Thursday's chip selloff.

items.detail: The **S&P 500** starts at a record **7,811.54**, and Thursday's producer prices and retail sales follow CPI as bank earnings season begins.
items.why: Firm spending with hot prices would back higher-for-longer rates and weigh on rate-sensitive stocks.

items.detail: **China's September CPI on Wednesday** comes after August's soft **0.5%**, and **TSMC's results Thursday** set the tone for Taiwan and Korea's chip-heavy markets.
items.why: Weak Chinese prices and a stronger dollar after a hot US CPI would extend Asia's oil-driven selloff.

items.detail: **HCLTech reports Monday**, opening India's IT earnings season, with the **Nifty** at **22,520** after last week's 52-week low and RBI hike.
items.why: Strong deal wins would steady IT stocks, but foreign selling depends more on crude and US yields.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** enters at **2,806.98**, about 9% below its August high, with Wednesday's CPI and Thursday's retail sales its key tests.
items.why: Small firms carry more floating-rate debt, so a hot print that lifts yields hurts them most.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** enters near **$82,600** after twice failing at $87,000, and **Wednesday's US CPI** is the main scheduled catalyst.
items.why: Another week of ETF outflows after a hot print could retest $81,000; a soft one may slow them.

items.detail: **Ether** starts near **$2,500**, with no confirmed Glamsterdam mainnet date, so ETF flows and **Wednesday's CPI** drive the week.
items.why: An end to eight straight days of ETF outflows is needed to hold above last week's $2,406 low.

items.detail: **Solana** enters near **$110** after breaking below its $120 range, with Solana ETF flows and **Wednesday's CPI** as the swing factors.
items.why: Solana tends to fall harder than bitcoin, so a hot print and more outflows could extend the slide.

items.detail: **Spot gold** starts near **$4,194**, just under $4,200, with **Wednesday's US CPI** the catalyst most likely to move it.
items.why: A hot print lifts yields and the dollar, hurting gold; a soft one could clear $4,200.

crossCuttingTheme: Wednesday's US CPI will test whether last week's oil spike is feeding into inflation: a hot print would lift yields and the dollar, pressuring tech, emerging markets, small caps, crypto and gold together.
